text:
Seattle's defense has leaned hard on Brandon Montour. He's playing 24:05 a night, he topped 30 minutes against Detroit, and he has 12 points in 17 games. Alison Lukan called him "a tone setter" after the overtime win over Calgary.

There is some luck in the scoring. He's shooting 9.4%, above our range for him, his scoring rate is just past the top of the band we'd expect, and the Kraken have scored about four more goals than expected with him on the ice. Last season ran the other way: Evolving-Hockey had his chances worth 1.4 expected wins against -0.2 actual, so some of this is the bounces evening out.

The engine is still elite. NHL EDGE has him in the 98th percentile for 20-plus mph bursts and the 88th for shot speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 31% of his shots coming off the rush last season, nearly double a typical defenseman. He lives in transition.

The team around him is the problem. At five-on-five Seattle has 45% of the shot attempts in his minutes, and the Kraken came home from the Global Series in Finland with two losses to Carolina.
